newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up, but liquidity low.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up, but liquidity low.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed a shade up on Wednesday, but turnover was held down due to low liquidity and lack of sellers, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.5 points up at 630.4, in keeping with this year's upward trend.
But turnover was a low 32.4 million rupees as would-be sellers refused to budge, anticipating that the market was going to hold strong in coming months, brokers said.
"There is a problem of sourcing sellers for blue chips, though buyers have lined up looking for sellers," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Commercial Stock Brokers.
Gunewardena said there was general expectation among many investors that the market was firm and was unlikely to come down. "So many don't want to sell and get out," he said.
On Wednesday, losses eged gains 22 to 19. Blue chip Hayleys was up four rupes to 190 rupees. Commercial Bank was up 25 cents to 150.75. Lanka Tiles was down 1.75 to 20.75.
The market is closed on Thursday for a public holiday.
